---
title: "Self-check: reading organic structures"
---

Answer before opening each check. Give a reason or a drawing, not only a term.

## 1. How many carbons are in a zigzag with four line segments and no branches?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check your answer"}
Five: one at each of the two endpoints and three internal vertices. Saturated acyclic neutral pentane is C₅H₁₂.
:::

## 2. Does C₂H₆O establish that a sample is ethanol?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check your answer"}
No. Dimethyl ether shares that molecular formula. Connectivity or suitable experimental evidence is needed.
:::

## 3. How many oxygen atoms are in CH₃C(=O)OH?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check your answer"}
Two. One is double-bonded to carbon; the other is single-bonded to carbon and H.
:::

## 4. What charge has oxygen with one single bond and three lone pairs?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check your answer"}
Formal charge −1: 6 − 6 − 1 = −1. Hydroxide is an example.
:::

## 5. Does a wedge add a fifth bond to carbon?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check your answer"}
No. It describes one bond pointing toward the viewer. Carbon still obeys its valence requirements.
:::

## 6. Convert 1.3812 g using molar mass 138.12 g/mol.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check your answer"}
The amount is 0.01000 mol = 10.00 mmol. Dividing grams by grams per mole gives moles.
:::
